podcast.body: This album was the biggest selling rock CD in all of America in 2009, with sales of 1.4 million copies. Its commercial performance highlighted the continued decline in rock album sales, even for top-performing acts. "And they sold just 1.4 million copies of only by the night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Alt Rock Chapter: 15

podcast.body: This album, Kings of Leon's fourth, was the record that truly propelled the band to mainstream success, with the single "Notion" being a major hit. For some fans, it seemed the band "came out of nowhere" with this album, though the band points out it took five years, one EP, and four albums to reach this level of fame. They found it particularly satisfying to reach big venues with their fourth album, having "worked their way up" rather than achieving instant success. "One of the big singles from their 2008 album, Only by the Knights, the record that really pushed him over the top."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Kings of Leon in Their Own Words: Part 1

podcast.body: This fourth album represented a significant breakthrough for Kings of Leon, serving as a payoff for the patience shown by their record label in allowing them to develop. It notably featured the hit song "Sex on Fire," which Nathan Followell initially voted against for inclusion on the album but was ultimately outvoted by the other members. "All of this patience really paid off with the fourth album only by the night."
